text:
maya: CI red on `hetero-nightly` - lots of warmup OOMs and a weird driver mismatch in logs. filing for quick triage, can someone grab a rerun and/or bisect?
jon: saw this too, kicked a rerun but flaky. repro only on mig shards and hetero pool.
sandeep: can you paste the error snippet?
maya: sure, here's the tail from the failing shard:```
[2024-11-09T02:14:33Z] runtime error: invalid device function
[2024-11-09T02:14:33Z] cudaInit failed: driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime
[2024-11-09T02:14:34Z] warmup: OOM allocating 512MB for KV cache
```
amelia: interesting — driver mismatch + OOM on the same run suggests node had a transient driver bump or stale user image. which image tag?
maya: image `redwood/ci:pr-4523-quant` on node hetero-3 (a100 + l40 mix).
jon: ugh that tag was built on canary infra with newer driver 536. I'm guessing the node kernel/driver is 535 and the image was compiled against 536 symbols.
sandeep: @maya can you run `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i driver` output from the failed node? also paste the full `dmesg | tail` if available.
maya: pasted from logs:```
--- nvidia-smi ---
Driver Version: 535.86.10
CUDA Version: 12.2
--- dmesg tail ---
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: API mismatch: the client has the version 536.25 but the kernel module has version 535.86.10
[ 1234.567891] NVRM: GPU fell off the bus
```
amelia: yep that API mismatch. we should avoid running images built against driver 536 on nodes with 535. Two quick options: pin the image runtime driver or rerun on canary nodes with 536.
jon: for quick triage can we isolate whether OOMs still occur if driver mismatch is fixed? request: rerun same job on `hetero-canary-2` and also rerun on `hetero-3` after a driver reload.
ci-bot: rerun requested by @jon: job pr-4523 on queues [hetero-canary-2, hetero-3]. status: queued.
ops-bot: note: driver reload on hetero-3 requires node reboot; scheduling maintenance window in 15m if no objections.
sandeep: i'll pick the bisect if reruns on both nodes show different failure modes. maya — could you attach the failing test id? makes automated rerun mapping easier.
maya: test id `tests/e2e/warmup/test_kv_cache.py::TestKVCache::test_warmup_under_load` from shard 7.
jon: adding quick bisect plan: 1) rerun on canary-2 (expected: no driver mismatch; check OOM) 2) rerun on hetero-3 after reboot (expected: driver matches; check OOM) 3) if OOM persists, bisect commits between last-green and HEAD for memory regression with `git bisect run ./ci/scripts/run_warmup_test.sh`.
sandeep: sounds good. for step 3 i'll prep a short bisect script that runs the single test with `--repeat 3` to filter flakes.
ci-bot: rerun started on hetero-canary-2 (job 4523-rerun-1).
ci-bot: rerun started on hetero-3 (job 4523-rerun-2).
maya: thanks. will watch logs. if hetero-canary-2 passes and hetero-3 fails with API mismatch, we can close on driver skew.
[~18m later]
ci-bot: job 4523-rerun-1 (hetero-canary-2) finished: PASS (warmup test passed, no OOM).
ci-bot: job 4523-rerun-2 (hetero-3) finished: FAIL (same driver API mismatch + warmup OOM).
jon: confirmed — hetero-3 is still on 535 kernel module. ops-bot any update on reboot?
ops-bot: reboot completed; driver module updated to 536.25 on hetero-3.
ci-bot: queued rerun on hetero-3 after maintenance (job 4523-rerun-3).
ci-bot: job 4523-rerun-3 finished: PASS (no OOM, warmup stable).
maya: great — root cause: driver skew between build environment and node kernel module.
jon: follow-ups: 1) add a check in CI canary matrix to skip nodes with driver < required, 2) add image metadata label `build-driver-version` so scheduler can match images to nodes, 3) ops: periodic driver drift detection alert.
sandeep: i'll open a tiny PR for the scheduler label match and add a CI guard in `ci/runner.py` to validate driver compatibility before test boot. assigning to me.
amelia: i'll file the ops ticket for driver drift detection and schedule rolling upgrades for hetero pool.
maya: thanks everyone. closing triage — @sandeep please ping when bisect script PR is up if needed. :thumbsup:
